given: active Organization with an un-lapsed Subscription and an actor holding staff authority
when: the actor invites a person by email address
then: membership is written active immediately, an invitation is written pending, and an audit record naming the actor is written, all in one transaction

situation: Invite with a role and Properties at once
given: same as SP-S1-01 and the form names a role and two Properties
when: the actor invites
then: the membership, the role and both assignments are written together or not at all

situation: Invite somebody already in this Organization
given: an active or revoked membership already exists for that user and Organization
when: the actor invites them again
then: refused: one person has one membership per Organization

situation: Invite into an Organization the actor does not reach
given: actor holds staff authority in Organization A
when: the actor invites into Organization B
then: refused and indistinguishable from the Organization not existing

given: the Organization's Subscription is suspended
when: the actor invites
then: refused by the commercial gate before anything is written

given: active Organization and the form names no Property
when: the actor invites
then: membership is active and reaches nothing, which is a normal state and shown as such on the roster

given: a pending invitation exists and the membership is already active
when: the person sets a password
then: they can sign in, the invitation becomes accepted, and the membership is unchanged because it was never waiting

given: the membership was revoked before the person accepted
when: the person opens the link and sets a password
then: refused: the invitation is withdrawn and no session is issued

given: an active membership holding a shipped role
when: the actor changes it to another role
then: the role changes, every session that Staff Member holds ends, and an audit record is written, whether the role is one Ranza ships or one the Organization authored, from the roster as from the module
test_name: changing_a_role_ends_their_sessions; staff.spec.ts: an administrator changes somebody's role from the roster

given: a role authored by Organization B
when: the actor in Organization A assigns it
then: unrepresentable: a role reference carries the Organization and a composite foreign key proves the pair

given: an active membership with two Property assignments
when: the actor revokes it
then: the membership and both assignments become revoked, every session ends, and nothing is deleted

given: exactly one active membership holds staff authority
when: the actor revokes or demotes it
then: refused: an Organization always has somebody who can add staff

situation: Two Owners demote each other at once
given: two active memberships hold staff authority and two transactions start together
when: both demotions commit
then: exactly one succeeds and the other is refused, because the trigger locks the Organization's memberships rather than counting them

given: a membership revoked a moment ago
when: the actor undoes the revoke
then: the same membership row returns to active with its assignments, so the person is one thread before and after

given: a membership revoked long enough ago
when: the actor undoes the revoke
then: refused: after the window it takes a fresh invitation

given: a membership revoked after the window closed
when: the actor invites them again
then: the same row returns to active and a new invitation is written, because one person has one membership per Organization

situation: Assigning a Property of another Organization
given: a Property belonging to Organization B
when: the actor in Organization A assigns it
then: unrepresentable: the assignment carries organization_id and the composite foreign key proves the pair

given: an active assignment
when: the actor removes it
then: the assignment becomes revoked, the row stays as the record that they used to reach it, and sessions end

given: an assignment revoked earlier
when: the actor assigns the same Property again
then: the same row returns to active

given: any active membership in the Organization
when: the Staff Member opens the screen
then: they see every Staff Member of their own Organization, and none of another's

situation: Does a lapsed Subscription block revoking
given: SP-S1-05 refuses an invite when the Subscription has lapsed
when: the actor revokes a compromised account while lapsed
then: removing reach is never blocked by money: the commercial gates apply to invite, assign, change_role, define and edit, and not to revoke, unassign or retire. Blocking a revoke turns an unpaid invoice into a security incident.

situation: How long the undo window is
given: SP-S1-15 refuses an undo after a window
when: the actor asks how long they have
then: the window is 24 hours of wall clock from revoked_at, carried in the update's own predicate so a late undo returns no row rather than raising. An Organization has no business date and ADR 0021 is about Properties, so wall clock is the only clock there is.

given: states.mmd draws an expire transition
when: a pending invitation is never accepted
then: an invitation expires seven days after it is written. A password-setting link that never expires is a standing credential. The membership is untouched by the expiry because it was never waiting on it, and re-inviting writes a fresh invitation against the same membership.

given: the actor holds staff authority and is not the only one who does
when: the actor changes their own role
then: allowed, and their own sessions end with everybody else's

given: an active membership with no assignment and no Organization-wide scope
when: the person signs in
then: the workspace opens empty and says so, rather than looking broken

situation: Getting the invitation to the person
given: no notification module exists and blueprint 5.12 specifies one
when: the actor invites somebody and there is no way to send an email
then: the invitation link is shown to the actor who created it, to pass on by hand. Notifications (blueprint 5.12) replaces that when it exists; until then this is honest and it is one field on a screen.

given: a membership is revoked while its invitation is still pending
when: the actor revokes
then: the invitation becomes withdrawn in the same transaction, so a live link cannot outlive the job it was for

situation: Assigning a Property to somebody already here
given: an active membership with no assignment to that Property
when: the actor assigns it
then: the assignment is written active and every session that Staff Member holds ends

given: a command changed a membership, a role or an assignment
when: the transaction commits
then: staff.reach_changed is published in the same transaction carrying ids and no names, so a session that should have ended cannot be lost by the handler not existing yet

given: a role is a named set of permissions
when: the gate asks whether this actor may run this command
then: every command in the product is a row in public.staff_permissions and a role holds a subset of it; a permission that is not in the catalogue is refused, so a typo in a role editor is a refusal rather than a role that silently grants nothing

situation: A command the role does not permit
given: the actor reaches the Property and holds a role without that permission
when: the actor runs the command
then: refused in the database beside blueprint 3.5's four gates rather than by the screen declining to draw a button

situation: Reading what each role may do
given: any active membership
when: the Staff Member opens the grid
then: they see every role of their Organization and the shipped ones, and none authored by another Organization

situation: A fifth gate beside the four
given: ADR 0012 says a write policy carries all four of blueprint 3.5's gates
when: the permission gate is added
then: the permission gate is a fifth condition inside the existing write policies rather than a second mechanism beside them, and ADR 0012 is amended to say so rather than contradicted by a new ADR. Amending every policy already written is part of s2 and not a later tidy-up.

situation: May an author grant what they do not hold
given: the actor defines a role from the catalogue
when: the actor includes a permission their own role lacks
then: refused: an author may only include permissions their own role holds. Otherwise defining a role is privilege escalation with extra steps. The Owner role Ranza ships holds the whole catalogue, so nothing is unreachable.

given: an Organization's own role held by three Staff Members
when: the actor retires it
then: refused while anybody holds it. Moving people automatically decides their permissions for them silently; refusing makes the actor reassign them first, where it is visible. The same shape as the ON DELETE RESTRICT this schema uses everywhere else.

situation: Defining a role without a name
given: the actor opens the role editor
when: the actor saves with the name empty
then: refused: a new set of permissions is a new role and a role is named

given: Organization A already has a role called Night manager
when: the actor defines another with that name
then: refused: a name is unique within the Organization

given: the actor opens a shipped role
when: the actor changes what it may do
then: refused: shipped roles arrive in a release and are the fixed reference every Organization shares

given: the actor opens a shipped role
when: the actor retires it
then: refused for the same reason as SP-S3-05

given: Organization B authored a role
when: Organization A opens the grid
then: it is absent, and absent is indistinguishable from never having existed

given: the actor opens the role editor with a name and a set of permissions
when: the actor saves
then: the role is written active, owned by this Organization, and an audit record names the author

given: a role this Organization authored and three Staff Members hold
when: the actor changes what it may do
then: the role changes and the sessions of everybody holding it end, because what they may do has changed

given: a role this Organization authored and nobody holds
when: the actor retires it
then: the role becomes retired and stays, because it is the record of what somebody used to be able to do

given: a retired role this Organization authored
when: the actor reinstates it
then: the same role returns to active and may be held again

given: ranza_app is granted nothing on auth_session and credentials are reached through ranza_auth by design
when: a reach change requires every session of that Staff Member to end
then: ranza_worker is granted EXECUTE on app.end_sessions_for(uuid) and no grant on any auth table: it can say end every session this Ranza user holds and nothing else. ADR 0005 is unchanged rather than amended — see ADR 0027.

situation: Every session and not only one
given: a Staff Member signed in on a desk terminal and a phone
when: the actor changes their role
then: every session ends, not the one that happens to be making the request

given: app.identify_staff_user is security definer and granted to ranza_app
when: anything holding the runtime role calls it
then: it refuses unless the caller holds staff.administer in the Organization named AND the Organization can use platform_core/staff_administration — both gates the membership INSERT applies, asked before the lookup and before the insert. A definer bypasses row-level security, so it asks what the policy would have asked. The capability is there as well as the permission because checking the permission alone leaves the same hole for a lapsed Subscription: the caller is an administrator, the policy refuses on money, and the row is written anyway. Note the invite path alone does not prove this - it runs in a transaction, so a refused INSERT rolls the row back - which is why the assertion calls the function directly

given: staff_invitations.token_hash holds a SHA-256 of 32 random bytes, on a unique index
when: somebody asks for a constant-time comparison instead of =
then: not done, and recorded so it is not re-opened. A perfect timing oracle on the comparison yields the stored HASH, and using it needs a preimage - which is the whole reason a token is hashed at rest. The alternative costs the unique index: a constant-time comparator has to scan every row of staff_invitations on every attempt. Real O(n) cost for a channel that leads nowhere. Reopen only if the token stops being hashed or stops being 256 bits of randomness

situation: What accepting an invitation is allowed to mean
given: the membership is written active at invite (SP-S1-01), acceptance only records it (SP-S1-07), nothing reads accepted_at and no route is wired to app.accept_staff_invitation
when: somebody presents a token they were not sent
then: harmless TODAY, and only today: acceptance grants nothing because nothing was withheld. This row is the condition. If anything ever gates on accepted_at, or acceptance is wired to a route, the caller's identity must be checked against invitation.user_id in the same change - otherwise a leaked token becomes a membership the day acceptance starts meaning something. Nothing currently checks who is calling, so the guard has to arrive with the meaning

situation: A definer that is handed a user id and asked to end their sessions
given: app.end_sessions_for() is SECURITY DEFINER, deletes from public.auth_session, and is granted to ranza_worker alone — which bounds who may call it and says nothing about which user they may name. Its owner carries BYPASSRLS in both environments, so no policy stops it.
when: a worker calls it with a user id from an event payload
then: PROPOSED. It refuses outside a worker context, because app.set_worker_context() is executable by ranza_worker and nobody else, so a caller without one did not come through the dispatcher. It then refuses a user the context's Organization has no membership row for — every status, not active, because a reach change is usually a revocation and narrowing to active would make the check inert in exactly the case it exists for. Found by IG-12's sweep when chore/insert-grants merged; neither branch's CI could see it.

situation: A definer that accepts an invitation and asks nothing about who presented it
given: app.accept_staff_invitation() is SECURITY DEFINER, writes to staff_invitations and organization_memberships, and takes only a token hash. Accepting grants nothing: the membership is written active at invite time (SP-S1-01) and acceptance only records that it happened (SP-S1-07).
when: a caller presents a token hash that is not theirs
then: PROPOSED, and weaker than SP-S4-03 on purpose. This closes no hole — 20260916002700 already reasoned that nothing here is an authorization boundary, and that is still right. It becomes a tripwire so the IG-12 sweep can assert zero writers-without-a-check rather than keep an exception list. The rule is conditional because the flow deliberately runs with NO request context (the invitee may not be able to sign in yet, and the token is the authentication): if a context is set at all, it must be the invitee's. The no-context arm is asserted too, because a guard that refused the real path would be worse than the absence it replaced. A token matching nothing still returns no row rather than an error, so withdrawn, expired, used and never-existed stay one answer.

situation: Handing out a role above your own
given: an administrator whose role holds staff.administer but not the whole catalogue — for instance a role an Owner authored holding staff.administer alone
when: they assign themselves or a colleague a role, or invite somebody with one
then: refused unless every permission in the role assigned is one their own role holds, whether the role is shipped or the Organization's own — the same ceiling SP-S3-01 puts on defining a role, which assigning could otherwise walk around in one step. Revoking is never refused (SP-S1-21). A demotion to a role they may not grant is refused like granting it, because a policy sees only the row as it will be; they may revoke instead
test_name: staff_and_permissions.test.sql: an administrator whose role is narrower than Owner cannot make themselves Owner; staff.test.ts: refuses a holder of staff.administer alone making themselves Owner; still lets them revoke somebody whose role they could not grant
